from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Nature of Light", [
            "Light behaves as a transverse electromagnetic wave.",
            "A polarizer acts like a vertical slotted fence.",
            "Only light oscillating in the plane passes through."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Create a light wave (represented as a line/wave pattern)
        light_wave = VGroup(*[Line(UP*0.5, DOWN*0.5, color="#FFFFFF") for _ in range(10)])
        light_wave.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        self.place_at_grid(light_wave, 'B3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(light_wave))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        polarizer = Rectangle(height=3, width=0.1, color="#FF00FF", fill_opacity=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(polarizer, 'C4', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(Create(polarizer))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF00FF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Filtered light
        filtered_light = light_wave.copy().set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(light_wave.copy(), filtered_light),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Mechanism: Optical Activity", [
            "Sugar molecules have a chiral, asymmetric structure.",
            "These molecules force polarized light to rotate.",
            "This rotation is known as optical activity."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display incoming polarized light
        # A simple arrow representing the polarization vector
        pol_light = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP*0.5, color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(pol_light, 'B2')
        self.play(Create(pol_light))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Introduce a chiral molecule
        molecule = VGroup(
            Circle(radius=0.2, color="#FF00FF", fill_opacity=0.5),
            Dot(color="#FFFFFF")
        )
        self.place_at_grid(molecule, 'B4')
        self.play(FadeIn(molecule))
        
        # Animate rotation
        self.play(Rotate(pol_light, angle=PI/4, about_point=self.grid['B2']))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF00FF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Show progressive angular shift
        final_arrow = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=rotate_vector(UP*0.5, PI/2), color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(final_arrow, 'B2')
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(pol_light, final_arrow))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Creating the 'Barber Pole' Effect", [
            "We use a polarized light and sugar solution.",
            "Light rotates differently based on its wavelength.",
            "This creates a helical, barber pole pattern.",
            "An analyzer reveals these vibrant color bands.",
            "The cylinder appears as a stack of colors."
        ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show multiple stacked polarizers at slight angles in #00FFFF.
        polarizers = VGroup(*[Rectangle(width=2, height=0.5, color="#00FFFF") for _ in range(3)])
        polarizers.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.2)
        self.place_at_grid(polarizers, "B2", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(polarizers))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Animate light passing through each, showing progressive rotation.
        light_beam = Line(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*2, color="#FFFF00").rotate(0.1, about_point=ORIGIN)
        self.place_at_grid(light_beam, "C3", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(light_beam), light_beam.animate.rotate(0.5, about_point=light_beam.get_start()))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight the resulting 'barber pole' spiral shape in #FF00FF.
        spiral = ParametricFunction(
            lambda t: np.array([np.sin(t*5), t, np.cos(t*5)]) * 0.5,
            t_range=np.array([0, 4]),
            color="#FF00FF"
        )
        self.place_at_grid(spiral, "D4", scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(Create(spiral))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF00FF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Malus's Law dictates the light intensity output.",
            "Varying sugar concentration changes the helix pitch.",
            "A graph maps depth to rotation angles.",
            "Periodic curves define the observed spectral colors.",
            "Rotation correlates directly to sugar concentration depth."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Mathematical Visualization", lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors for lecture lines
        colors = ["#FF6B6B", "#4ECDC4", "#FFE66D", "#FF9F1C", "#A29BFE"]
        
        # Setup objects
        # Rotating Vector
        vec = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT, color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(vec, 'B2', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Wave Function Graph
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[-1.5, 1.5, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        wave = axes.plot(lambda x: np.cos(x), color="#FFE66D")
        graph_group = VGroup(axes, wave)
        self.place_at_grid(graph_group, 'E4', scale_factor=0.5)

        # Equations
        malus_eq = MathTex(r"I = I_0 \cos^2(\theta)", color="#FF6B6B")
        self.place_at_grid(malus_eq, 'D2', scale_factor=0.7)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(colors[0]))
        self.play(Create(malus_eq))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(colors[1]))
        # Animate helix pitch change (simulation)
        self.play(vec.animate.rotate(PI/4))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(colors[2]))
        self.play(Create(graph_group))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(colors[3]))
        self.play(wave.animate.set_color("#FF9F1C"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(colors[4]))
        self.play(vec.animate.rotate(PI/4))

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Real-World Application", [
            "Polarimetry measures sugar concentration without samples.",
            "Industries use this to maintain syrup quality.",
            "Lasers verify batch concentration instantly, non-destructively."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        tube = Cylinder(radius=0.4, height=3, color="#55AAFF", fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(tube, 'C3', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        laser_beam = Line(start=LEFT*2, end=RIGHT*2, color="#FF4444")
        self.place_at_grid(laser_beam, 'C3', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        reading = MathTex(r"0.0^\circ").set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(reading, 'E3', scale_factor=1.2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(tube), FadeIn(laser_beam))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#55AAFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        rotation_group = VGroup(laser_beam.copy())
        self.play(Rotate(laser_beam, angle=PI/4, about_point=self.grid['C3']))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF55")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        reading.become(MathTex(r"12.5^\circ").set_color("#FF55FF"))
        self.place_at_grid(reading, 'E3', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(FadeIn(reading))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF55FF")
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Barber Pole Effect: Polarized Light in Sugar Solutions

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Nature of Light
sections.content: Briefly define light as a transverse electromagnetic wave. Introduce the concept of a polarization filter as a 'slotted fence' that only allows waves oscillating in a specific plane to pass through.
sections.example: Visualizing a rope being shaken through a vertical picket fence—only vertical waves pass, horizontal waves are blocked.

sections.title: The Mechanism: Optical Activity
sections.content: Explain that sugar molecules are 'chiral' (asymmetric). When polarized light passes through a sugar solution, the interaction with these chiral molecules forces the plane of polarization to rotate. This is called optical rotation.
sections.example: An animation showing a light wave vector rotating like a corkscrew as it travels through a tank of sugar water.

sections.title: Creating the 'Barber Pole' Effect
sections.content: Describe the setup: A light source, a polarizer, a tall cylinder of concentrated sugar solution, and a rotating analyzer (second polarizer). As the light travels deeper into the solution, different wavelengths rotate by different amounts (dispersion), creating a stack of colors.
sections.example: When viewing the cylinder through the analyzer, a multi-colored helical pattern emerges, resembling the stripes of a rotating barber pole.

sections.title: Mathematical Visualization
sections.content: Introduce Malus's Law (I = I0 cos²θ). Use a circular vector diagram where θ represents the rotation angle, showing how varying the concentration of sugar changes the 'pitch' of the helical color bands.
sections.example: A graph overlaying the cylinder: X-axis represents depth, Y-axis represents rotation angle. As you move along the depth, the light intensity at the analyzer follows a periodic cos² curve, mapping to different spectral colors.

sections.title: Real-World Application
sections.content: Conclude with how this phenomenon, known as polarimetry, is used in the food and medical industries to measure sugar concentration (Brix) accurately without destroying the sample.
sections.example: A quality control robot in a soda factory using a laser polarimeter to instantly verify the exact sugar percentage in every batch of syrup.
